attempts.raw_response: Baby’s breath, lavender, and waxflower are popular filler choices that add texture and volume without overpowering the main blooms. Before assembling, decide on the headdress style—a crown, a halo, or a side piece—and measure the circumference where it will sit. For a secure fit, attach the flowers to a sturdy base like floral wire, a headband, or a ribbon. Use floral tape to bind stems tightly, and trim excess length. If using fresh flowers, keep them hydrated by misting lightly until the event. For a longer-lasting option, dried or silk flowers work beautifully and can be prepared weeks in advance. Finish with a few sprigs of greenery for a natural, cohesive look.

pair.human_continuation: While you can certainly make a floral headdress using only your main flowers, adding filler flowers is a great option if you want to add more color and visual interest to your headdress.  Baby’s breath, poms, and statice make great options for filler flowers.  Depending on the size of the flowers and the bunches they are sold in, you will likely need 1 or 2 bunches of filler flowers. Like filler flowers, greenery adds visual interest to your floral headdress. Adding greenery is also helpful if you want to disguise the florist wire base of your headdress and hide it from view. Ivy, eucalyptus, and ferns are some great greenery options. These plants have long and bendable stems or leaves, making them easy to wrap around the florist wire base.
pair.prefix: You can use real or fake flowers depending on the occasion and your personal preference. Choose one main flower for your headdress, or mix it up with 2 or 3 options. Roses, dahlias, daisies, carnations, and peonies are all great options that tend to hold up well on floral headdresses. Filler flowers are smaller flowers that can be used to fill in any dead space on your floral headdress.
